background_story: Adelaide was a brilliant physicist who spent most of her career studying the mysteries of electricity. Growing up in a family of inventors, she was fascinated by the workings of the electrometer, an instrument used to measure the strength of electric currents. Her groundbreaking research on the device led to the development of a new, more accurate model that revolutionized the field of electrical engineering. Adelaide's work took her to the esteemed laboratories of Cambridge University, where she collaborated with other prominent scientists to explore the applications of electrometry in medicine and technology. Her contributions earned her numerous accolades, including the prestigious Maxwell Award, solidifying her reputation as a leading expert in the field. Adelaide's work with the electrometer paved the way for major breakthroughs in our understanding of the natural world.
